title: What's it like to be a twin?
speaker: BBC Learning English

keywords.def: (idiom) move your eyes upwards as a way of showing you are annoyed or bored by what someone has said
significant stage or event in the development of something
used to describe two people who are unusually similar or connected; or siblings who were separated and adopted by different parents at birth
strange in a frightening and mysterious way

sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好，这里是BBC学英语的6分钟英语节目。

sentences.en: I'm Neil. And I'm Beth. In this episode, we're talking about twins.
sentences.zh: 我是尼尔。我是贝丝。在本期节目中，我们来聊聊双胞胎。

sentences.en: Non-identical, or fraternal, twins come from two separate eggs and share half their genes.
sentences.zh: 非同卵双胞胎（即异卵双胞胎）来自两个不同的卵子，共享一半的基因。

sentences.en: More uncommon are identical twins, who come from a single fertilised egg and share 100% of their genes.
sentences.zh: 更少见的是同卵双胞胎，他们来自一个受精卵，共享100%的基因。

sentences.en: As humans, we're fascinated by twins. When people discover that someone's a twin, they start asking all kinds of questions.
sentences.zh: 作为人类，我们对双胞胎充满了好奇。当人们发现某人是双胞胎时，就会开始问各种各样的问题。

sentences.en: What question would you ask a twin, Neil?
sentences.zh: 你会问双胞胎什么问题呢，尼尔？

sentences.en: Oh, probably quite an annoying one. Maybe… "Do you share each other's thoughts?"
sentences.zh: 哦，可能会是个挺烦人的问题。比如……“你们能共享彼此的想法吗？”

sentences.en: Ooh! I might ask, "If one of you is hurt, does the other one feel the pain?"
sentences.zh: 噢！我可能会问，“如果你们其中一个受伤了，另一个会感觉到痛吗？”

sentences.en: Hmm. Interesting. Well, some common questions for twins include: "Do you have psychic powers?
sentences.zh: 嗯。很有意思。好吧，人们对双胞胎常问的问题包括：“你们有特异功能吗？

sentences.en: Have you ever swapped boyfriends? And do you have the same dreams?" But according to Anand Jagatia, who presented a recent episode of BBC World Service's CrowdScience all about twins…
sentences.zh: 你们换过男朋友吗？你们会做同样的梦吗？”但根据Anand Jagatia的说法——他最近主持了BBC世界服务频道一档关于双胞胎的节目CrowdScience……

sentences.en: …if you meet a twin and you ask them one of these questions, don't be surprised if they roll their eyes at you.
sentences.zh: ……如果你遇到一个双胞胎并问了他们这些问题之一，当他们对你翻白眼时，别觉得惊讶。

sentences.en: Ask a twin about psychic powers and they might roll their eyes – a way of showing boredom or irritation.
sentences.zh: 问一个双胞胎关于特异功能的事，他们可能会翻白眼——这是一种表达无聊或烦躁的方式。

sentences.en: But nevertheless, twins continue to capture our imagination, and in this episode we'll be finding out why, using some useful new words and phrases.
sentences.zh: 不过尽管如此，双胞胎仍然吸引着我们的想象力，在本期节目中，我们将借助一些实用的新词汇和短语来探究原因。

sentences.en: And remember, you'll find all the vocabulary for this episode, along with a quiz and a worksheet, on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到本期的所有词汇、测验和练习页。

sentences.en: First, I have a question for you, Beth. These days, twins are more common than you might think.
sentences.zh: 首先，贝丝，我有一个问题考考你。如今，双胞胎比你想象的要常见。

sentences.en: In fact, one in every 42 babies is born a twin.
sentences.zh: 事实上，每42个婴儿中就有一个是双胞胎。

sentences.en: But do you know which famous Hollywood star is a twin?
sentences.zh: 但你知道哪个好莱坞明星是双胞胎吗？

sentences.en: Is it: a) Jennifer Lawrence, b) Angelina Jolie, or c) Scarlett Johansson?
sentences.zh: 是：a) 詹妮弗·劳伦斯，b) 安吉丽娜·朱莉，还是 c) 斯嘉丽·约翰逊？

sentences.en: Ooh, I don't know. I'm going to guess Scarlett Johansson.
sentences.zh: 噢，我不知道。我猜是斯嘉丽·约翰逊。

sentences.en: Well, we'll find out the answer at the end of the programme.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们在节目最后揭晓答案。

sentences.en: Professor Karen Dillon is the author of a book on twins in American literature and a twin herself.
sentences.zh: 凯伦·狄龙教授是一本关于美国文学中双胞胎的书的作者，她自己也是个双胞胎。

sentences.en: Here, she discusses the good and bad sides of twinship with Anand Jagatia, for BBC World Service programme CrowdScience: Being a twin isn't always plain sailing.
sentences.zh: 在这里，她与Anand Jagatia一起在BBC世界服务频道的节目CrowdScience中讨论了双胞胎生活的优缺点：当双胞胎并不总是一帆风顺的。

sentences.en: Yeah, it is nice – there's never that fear, because you're going through school together, you're sometimes in the same class together, you're making friends together.
sentences.zh: 对，其实挺好的——从来没有那种恐惧，因为你们一起经历学校生活，有时还在同一个班级，一起结交朋友。

sentences.en: So, all of those milestones of childhood, in some ways, are made easier for twins.
sentences.zh: 所以，童年的所有这些里程碑，在某种程度上对双胞胎来说更容易实现。

sentences.en: But then the older you get, the more you realise how much people really think of you as a twin rather than as an individual.
sentences.zh: 但接着你年纪越大，你就会越意识到人们有多么把你当成双胞胎，而不是作为一个独立的人来看待。

sentences.en: Twins go through many childhood milestones together.
sentences.zh: 双胞胎一起经历许多童年里程碑。

sentences.en: A milestone is an important stage of development, so a childhood milestone could be something like your first day at school.
sentences.zh: 里程碑是发展的重要阶段，所以童年的里程碑可能就像你上学的第一天这样的事情。

sentences.en: But being a twin isn't always plain sailing – an idiom meaning easy and problem-free.
sentences.zh: 但当双胞胎并不总是一帆风顺的——这是一个意为轻松且无问题（一帆风顺）的习语。

sentences.en: Many twins find it hard to establish their own identity as a separate and unique individual.
sentences.zh: 许多双胞胎发觉很难确立自己作为独立独特个体的身份。

sentences.en: Our fascination with twins also comes from the age-old 'nature versus nurture' debate: how much of our lives is determined by nature, the genetics we're born with, and how much by nurture, the environment we grow up in?
sentences.zh: 我们对双胞胎的迷恋也源于陈旧的“先天与后天”之争：我们生活中有多少是由先天（我们生来就有的基因）决定的，又有多少是由后天（我们成长的环境）决定的？

sentences.en: Because twins are so genetically similar, differences between them tell scientists a lot.
sentences.zh: 因为双胞胎在基因上如此相似，他们之间的差异能告诉科学家很多信息。

sentences.en: Here's presenter of BBC World Service programme CrowdScience, Anand Jagatia, discussing this with Helena De Bres, a philosopher at Wellesley College, Massachusetts, and – that's right – another twin.
sentences.zh: 这里是BBC世界服务频道CrowdScience节目的主持人Anand Jagatia，他正与马萨诸塞州韦尔斯利学院的哲学家、同时也是——没错——另一个双胞胎的Helena De Bres讨论这个问题。

sentences.en: Yeah, you hear about twins that were separated at birth, grew up in different parts of the world, and they kind of have these eerily similar life courses.
sentences.zh: 对，你听说过出生时就被分开的双胞胎，在世界不同地区长大，而他们有着这种诡异相似的人生轨迹。

sentences.en: And you think, "Gosh! How much choice have I had over the way my life's turned out?"
sentences.zh: 然后你会想，“天哪！对于我的人生如何走到这一步，我到底有多少选择权？”

sentences.en: Absolutely, yeah. There's that really famous case of the Jim Twins, who were reunited at age 39 after being separated at birth, and they just had so many similarities – it was crazy!
sentences.zh: 完全同意，是的。有一个非常著名的“吉姆双胞胎”的案例，他们在出生时分开后，39岁时团聚了，他们有着如此多的相似之处——太疯狂了！

sentences.en: They both married someone called Linda and then divorced her for someone called Betty.
sentences.zh: 他们都娶了一个叫琳达的人，然后又为了一个叫贝蒂的人跟她离婚。

sentences.en: They both named their dog 'Toy'. It was, like, ridiculous!
sentences.zh: 他们都给自己的狗起名叫“玩具”。这简直太荒谬了！

sentences.en: The twins, Jim Lewis and Jim Springer, were separated at birth.
sentences.zh: 这对双胞胎，吉姆·刘易斯和吉姆·斯普林格，出生时就被分开了。

sentences.en: The phrase separated at birth can be used to describe two people with strong similarities.
sentences.zh: 短语“出生时分离”可以用来描述两个有强烈相似之处的人。

sentences.en: Although, in this case the twins were literally separated and adopted by different parents at birth.
sentences.zh: 虽然在这个案例中，这对双胞胎确实是在出生时被不同的父母分开并收养的。

sentences.en: When the Jims were reunited in the 1970s, everyone was amazed at how similar their lives were.
sentences.zh: 当两位吉姆在20世纪70年代重聚时，所有人都对他们相似的人生惊叹不已。

sentences.en: Anand used the adjective eerie, meaning strange in a frightening, mysterious way.
sentences.zh: Anand使用了形容词eerie，意思是令人感到害怕、神秘般的奇怪。

sentences.en: And Helena says, "It was crazy," using crazy to mean strange and fantastic.
sentences.zh: 而海伦娜说，“这太疯狂了”，这里用crazy来表示奇怪又神奇。

sentences.en: Yes, I think 'strange', 'mysterious' and 'fantastic' describe being a twin quite well.
sentences.zh: 是的，我觉得“奇怪”、“神秘”和“神奇”把双胞胎的特质描述得很贴切。

sentences.en: OK. Neil, it's time to reveal the answer to your question.
sentences.zh: 好的。尼尔，是时候揭晓你那个问题的答案了。

sentences.en: I asked which Hollywood star is a twin, and you said, "c) Scarlett Johansson"… I did.
sentences.zh: 我问哪个好莱坞明星是双胞胎，你回答说“c) 斯嘉丽·约翰逊”……我确实是这么说的。

sentences.en: …which was the right answer. Yay! Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned, starting with roll your eyes – to move your eyes upwards to show you are bored or annoyed.
sentences.zh: ……这就是正确的答案。太棒了！让我们回顾一下学到的词汇，从“翻白眼”开始——向上转动眼睛以表现出你感到无聊或恼火。

sentences.en: A milestone is a significant stage in the development of something.
sentences.zh: 里程碑是事物发展中的一个重要阶段。

sentences.en: The idiom it's not plain sailing describes difficult and problematic situations.
sentences.zh: 习语“一帆风顺”描述的是困难和充满问题的境况。

sentences.en: The phrase separated at birth can describe two people who are unusually similar.
sentences.zh: 短语“出生时分离”可以描述两个异常相似的人。

sentences.en: It also refers to siblings who were adopted by different parents at birth.
sentences.zh: 它也指被不同父母收养的亲兄弟姐妹。

sentences.en: And the adjective eerie means strange in a frightening and mysterious way.
sentences.zh: 而形容词eerie的意思是带着可怕而神秘色彩的奇怪。

sentences.en: And finally,if someone says,"It was crazy!" they mean it was strange and fantastic.
sentences.zh: 最后，如果有人说，“太疯狂了！”，他们的意思是这又奇怪又神奇。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but remember – you can find worksheets, quizzes and loads more resources to improve your English on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟节目又到时间了，但请记住——你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到练习页、测验和更多用于提高英语水平的资源。

sentences.en: See you there soon, but for now – goodbye!
sentences.zh: 我们很快在那里再见，但现在——再见！

sentences.en: Goodbye!
sentences.zh: 再见！
